original_acceptance: Declaring a class method as `["\uD800"]() {}` registers it under an empty name, because HIR method names are Rust `String`s and the lone surrogate is lost. Calling it then fails. This is on main too, and was found while working on #12193. The fix is to carry method names as WTF-8 bytes, the same as runtime keys.
mapping: MemberName::Str(Vec<u8>) and member_name_of_value preserve raw key bytes instead of lossily decoding.
class_member_name/member_is_named and class_method_decl[_index]_bytes resolve exact declaration key.
class_prototype_method_value_for_bytes preserves exact key and computed function name.
native_call_method exact WTF-8 property lookup bypasses UTF-8 string-only dispatch.
Computed static methods materialize own shape properties; codegen method/name string pool updated.
test_gap_classsem_12202_class_wtf8_method.ts directly covers high/low surrogate and empty instance keys, static method, reflected names and anonymous class expression.
